title: System DLL loaded from a user-writable path
why: DLL search-order hijacking. Written from a Sysmon lab where a copied calc.exe loaded a planted WININET.dll.

title: .NET runtime loaded by a process that is not a .NET host
why: Unmanaged PowerShell: the CLR injected into a native process so PowerShell runs with no powershell.exe in the process log.

title: SSH password brute force from one source
why: Ten failed passwords from one address in five minutes, as a Sigma correlation rule. Ported from my log triage tool.

title: Client bypassing the filtering resolver with encrypted DNS
why: A device looks up a DNS-over-HTTPS or Private Relay bootstrap host, after which the resolver stops seeing it. Written after it happened on my own network.

title: Systemd unit written outside a package manager
why: A new service or timer unit appears, written by something that is not a package manager or systemd. Units are the usual way to survive a reboot on Linux. I write them by hand on my own server, so I know the normal noise: rare, and always an editor or a shell.

techniques.name: Create or modify system process: systemd service
